classification.classification_note: The scored GT is intentionally narrowed to the close-time write of uninitialized metadata bytes that the saved MSAN origin, store, and sink stacks directly prove. The staged patch hardens an earlier speculative object-header parser path, but the saved artifacts do not identify the exact dirty metadata client or serializer that bridged that path to the flushed 89-byte buffer.

analysis_state.reason: Reviewer feedback correctly rejected the previous end-to-end bridge from the `H5Ocache` speculative parser path to the sec2-driver sink. The rebuilt GT therefore scores only the source-grounded close-time chain that Stage 01 actually proves: `H5Fclose()` reaches `H5C__flush_single_entry()`, that function allocates the later-written buffer with `H5MM_malloc`, `H5F__accum_write()` copies bytes that still carry that allocation origin, and `H5FD__sec2_write()` consumes them. The exact dirty metadata client/serializer remains unidentified.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42521331 (hdf5): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target h5_extended_fuzzer [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42521331
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source snapshot
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` on the staged ARVO checkout `966454aac1231da7209ef81c11055d3312181f99`. The exact 1808-byte `poc` is written to disk, `H5Fopen(..., H5F_ACC_RDWR, ...)` accepts it, `H5Dopen2(..., "dsetname", ...)` emits the saved HDF5-DIAG object-header failure, and the harness still calls `H5Fclose()`. The rebuilt scored chain is intentionally narrower than that parser-side diagnostic: during `H5Fclose()`, `H5C__flush_single_entry()` allocates a fresh metadata image buffer with `H5MM_malloc` at line 6536, and the saved MSAN origin stack identifies that heap allocation as the creation point of the bytes later reported at the sink. The same close path then treats that buffer as the dirty entry's serialized on-disk image, `H5F__accum_write()` copies it into the metadata accumulator, and `H5FD__sec2_write()` passes it to `pwrite64`, where MSAN reports uninitialized bytes at offset 76 of an 89-byte write. The saved artifacts do not identify which dirty metadata client or client-specific serializer left those bytes untouched, so the staged `H5Ocache` patch is noted only as separate evidence and not used as the scored root cause of the observed sink.

source.description: First source-grounded materialization of the poisoned bytes on the proved close-time chain. `H5C__flush_single_entry()` allocates the heap buffer that later carries the uninitialized metadata bytes to the sink.
source.value_from: The exact 1808-byte HDF5 witness opens successfully in `H5F_ACC_RDWR`, and the saved MSAN origin stack shows that closing this file reaches `H5C__flush_single_entry()`, where this allocation creates the bytes later copied at `H5F__accum_write()` and consumed at `H5FD__sec2_write()`.

root_cause.description: Missing initialization obligation on the proved sink-side path: H5C allocates a fresh flush-image buffer with `H5MM_malloc` and later treats it as a complete serialized metadata image without first zero-initializing it.
root_cause.note: The saved artifacts do not identify the dirty metadata client or serializer for this entry, so the scored GT keeps the root cause at the generic source-level obligation MSAN directly proves: bytes from this fresh heap allocation survive into the later 89-byte sec2-driver write. The staged patch instead hardens an earlier `H5Ocache` parser path and is not scored here.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. The close-time metadata flush reaches the sec2 driver with `buf` still containing bytes that retain the allocation origin from `H5C__flush_single_entry()`.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `Uninitialized bytes in __interceptor_pwrite64 at offset 76 inside [0x709000003e78, 89)` and `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `/src/hdf5/src/H5FDsec2.c:836:27`.

parser_admitted.description: The exact witness has already been accepted by `H5Fopen(..., H5F_ACC_RDWR, ...)` and reaches the dataset-open attempt. The same harness function then still calls `H5Fclose(fuzz_h5_id)`, which is the control gate for the narrowed close-time flush chain.

tainted_value_origin.description: MSAN origin. The uninitialized bytes later copied into the accumulator and written by the sec2 driver originate in this heap allocation for the dirty entry's flush buffer.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The saved origin stack is `H5MM_malloc -> H5C__flush_single_entry -> H5C__flush_ring -> H5C_flush_cache -> H5AC_flush -> H5F__flush_phase2 -> H5F__dest -> H5Fclose`.

evidence_limitations: Stage 01 reproduced against workspace checkout `966454aac1231da7209ef81c11055d3312181f99`, not metadata vulnerable commit `a0340338e53d4b34127a7e5356b28b1640f9414c`; this checkout is an ancestor of both metadata commits and still contains the same vulnerable close-time flush path and the unfixed `H5Ocache.c` deserializer call sites.

The saved MSAN artifacts prove the allocation site at `src/H5C.c:6536`, the copy site at `src/H5Faccum.c:692`, and the sink at `src/H5FDsec2.c:836`, but they do not identify which dirty metadata client owned the flushed entry or which client-specific serializer left part of `entry_ptr->image_ptr` untouched before the write.

The saved HDF5-DIAG and patch diff still show a separate speculative object-header parser issue at `H5O__cache_get_final_load_size()` / `H5O__prefix_deserialize()`, but the current artifacts do not statically connect that parser-side path to the flushed 89-byte buffer. The rebuilt scored trace therefore excludes that earlier path rather than claiming an unsupported end-to-end bridge.
`run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, so Stage 02 did not instrument the ARVO workspace to identify the exact dirty metadata entry or serializer.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness writes the exact witness to disk, opens it with `H5F_ACC_RDWR`, attempts `H5Dopen2("dsetname")`, and still calls `H5Fclose()` after the saved dataset-open failure.
During close-time cache flush, H5C allocates a fresh heap image buffer for a dirty metadata entry. MSAN identifies this exact allocation as the origin of the bytes later reported at the sink.
The same `entry_ptr->image_ptr` buffer is treated as the dirty entry's on-disk image and copied into the metadata accumulator, even though some bytes still retain the step-2 heap allocation origin.
The sec2 driver writes the accumulator span, and MSAN reports uninitialized bytes at offset 76 inside an 89-byte `pwrite64`.

fine_trace.note: Harness step. The exact 1808-byte `poc` is written verbatim to a temporary file, opened `H5F_ACC_RDWR`, probed with `H5Dopen2("dsetname")`, and then closed if `H5Fopen()` succeeded. The saved run shows the file open succeeded, dataset open failed with HDF5-DIAG, and `H5Fclose()` still executed, which is the control fact that reaches the close-time flush chain.

Source, root cause, and MSAN origin for the narrowed chain. While flushing a dirty metadata entry on `H5Fclose()`, H5C allocates a fresh heap image buffer but does not initialize it. The saved MSAN origin trace identifies this allocation as the creation point of the bytes later copied and written; for the witnessed flush that buffer ultimately backs the 89-byte write reported at the sink.

The same heap buffer from step 2 is handed to the file-I/O layer as the dirty entry's metadata image. The saved artifacts do not identify the client-specific serializer for this entry, but the later MSAN origin still pointing to step 2 shows that some bytes in this write buffer were never overwritten after allocation.
MSAN's saved `stored to memory at` site. `H5F__accum_write()` copies the metadata bytes from step 3's `buf` into the metadata accumulator, so any still-uninitialized bytes now reside in `accum->buf`.
Sink. The dirty accumulator span is passed to the sec2 driver and `pwrite64` consumes it. The saved MSAN report says the uninitialized bytes are at offset 76 inside an 89-byte write.

allocation_context.note: The saved trace says the uninitialized value was created by `H5MM_malloc` at `src/H5MM.c:80`, invoked from this flush-buffer allocation site.

poc.trigger: Write the staged `poc` bytes to a temporary file, open it with `H5Fopen(..., H5F_ACC_RDWR, ...)`, attempt `H5Dopen2(..., "dsetname", ...)`, and then close the file. The verified trigger is that this close path reaches `H5C__flush_single_entry -> H5F__accum_write -> H5FD__sec2_write`, where MSAN reports uninitialized bytes in the 89-byte sec2-driver write.

format.name: HDF5
format.contract: Exactly the staged malformed 1808-byte HDF5 v5 file. The verified trigger facts are only that `H5Fopen()` accepts it in `H5F_ACC_RDWR`, the same run later reaches `H5Fclose()`, `H5C__flush_single_entry()` allocates the flushed metadata buffer named by MSAN's origin stack, and the close path then reaches the saved 89-byte `H5FD__sec2_write` with uninitialized bytes at offset 76. The saved object-header diagnostics and patch diff are separate evidence, not a claimed end-to-end cause of this scored sink.
